text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyWhen Frog Eyes Are Like FingerprintsThe eyes of egg-eating spiny-backed frogs certainly make an impressionDRBy Devin Reese11:00 AM CDT on October 28, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleWe have identification of humans down pat—a complete human fingerprint can pinpoint the person it belongs to more than 90 percent of the time, according to forensic scientists. To study animals in the wild, biologists also need to identify individuals, but they don’t have reliable proxies for fingerprints. That’s because, other than mammals, vertebrate animals lack unique ridge patterns on their fingers.But now, a study published in the journal Herpetozoa reports a reliable way to identify individual frogs without having to catch them. Typically, frog tissue samples for DNA analysis are clipped from the ends of toes. The capture and clipping can be stressful, however, especially for tree frogs, which use their toes to stick onto substrates. Read more: “The Secret Lives of Japanese Temple Frogs”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
